description.value: Functional MRI study of neural activation and functional connectivity during anticipation of fear faces in adults with inhibited versus uninhibited temperament, including correlations with social anxiety and emotion regulation scores.

spans.text: Functional MRI was used to measure brain activation during the anticipation of viewing fear faces in 34 young adults (17 inhibited, 17 uninhibited).

value: We hypothesized that the inhibited group would show greater activation of amygdala and insula during anticipation of fear faces, relative to the uninhibited group.

value: There were group differences in activation in the left insula and multiple prefrontal cortical regions, including the dorsal anterior cingulate, rostral anterior cingulate cortex, and bilateral dorsolateral prefrontal cortex.
During anticipation of viewing fear faces, relative to neutral faces, the inhibited subjects had greater activation in both the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and the dorsal ACC.

These findings show that the dACC was preferentially engaged during fear anticipation in the inhibited temperament group, whereas the insula showed lower activation during fear anticipation in the uninhibited group.

description.value: The Cognitive Emotion Regulation Questionnaire measured frequency of use of positive and negative cognitive emotion-regulation strategies.
